== main.c#L1-L31
     1  /* The harness for the compiled checker: the trusted C side of the end-to-end theorem.
     2  
     3     build:  make   (cc -std=gnu23 -O2 -pthread -o checker main.c checker.s; Makefile)
     4     usage:  checker [--jobs=N] FILE
     5  
     6     The default path is the one the final theorem covers (`checkerFile_accepts`,
     7     ConAgua/Final/EndToEnd.lean; the call is as `AbiCall` in ConAgua/Final/Abi.lean states it).
     8     It reads FILE (the input) whole into a buffer (`slurp`), maps one zero region of
     9     ca_region_size bytes, and calls, once,
    10  
    11       ca_start(in, in_len, pins, pins_len, region, region_len)
    12  
    13     with the pin data `pins` built into the binary (below). `ca_start` is the sequential driver:
    14     entry 1 (the stages and phase A), then entry 2 over every pending group, on the same region;
    15     the entry stubs lay out everything else inside the region. The verdict is one line on stdout,
    16     and the exit status follows the Lean kernel arena's convention (0 accepted, 1 rejected,
    17     2 declined, 3 error), claiming no more than the checker knows:
    18       accept      0  rdx = 0 and rax = ACCEPT (0x414343455054): the only accept
    19       error       2  rdx = 2: the checker aborted, which is a reject or a decline (it does not
    20                      tell them apart, so it claims neither: not accepted, nothing claimed)
    21       exhausted   2  rdx = 1: fuel, stack or region ran out (a resource limit; con-leche declines
    22                      when its fuel runs out)
    23       ok R        3  rdx = 0 and any other rax R, in decimal (1: the frontend rejected a malformed
    24                      line, which con-leche reports as an error too)
    25     A failure of the harness itself (usage, a file that cannot be read, no memory) prints a
    26     message on stderr and exits with status 3 and no verdict line. A crash (e.g. a page of the
    27     region the kernel cannot supply) prints nothing and ends with a signal. None is an accept.
    28  
    29     With --jobs=N for N > 1, the threaded mode, `run_jobs` below: its accept is covered by
    30     `checkerFile_threads_accept` (ConAgua/Final/EndToEnd.lean), under the hypotheses
    31     `ThreadsRun` (ConAgua/Final/ThreadsFinal.lean) states about this harness's threads. */

    90  or an unset register is never read as accept. -/

== ConAgua/Final/Twin.lean#L54-L64
    54  /-- **The twin accepts `chunks`**: the stages con-ron's binary runs, from the twin's start state
    55  `AState.init EStore.empty`, at some pin list, the fold on one worker. -/
    56  def TwinAccepts (chunks : List ByteArray) : Prop :=
    57    ∃ (pins : List NatOpPinSet) (sA sB sC sD sE sF : AState) (pre : PreludeIx) (r : ParseResultD)
    58      (ds : Array IDeclaration) (ipins : List INatOpPinSet) (fe : IFEnv),
    59      internReservedPins (AState.init EStore.empty) = .ok ((), sA) ∧
    60      builtinPreludeE sA = .ok (.ok pre, sB) ∧
    61      parseChunks chunks sB = .ok (.ok r, sC) ∧
    62      preparePrelude pre r.decls sC = .ok (ds, sD) ∧
    63      internAllPins pins sD = .ok (ipins, sE) ∧
    64      SeqAccepts .verified ipins ds sE fe sF

== ConAgua/Final/Twin.lean#L36-L42
    36  /-- **The x64 checker's fold**: phase A accepted with environment `fe` and pending records `pend`,
    37  ending in `s'`; phase B, every pending record in order on one worker made from `s'`, accepted. -/
    38  def SeqAccepts (mode : CheckMode) (pins : List INatOpPinSet) (ds : Array IDeclaration)
    39      (s : AState) (fe : IFEnv) (s' : AState) : Prop :=
    40    ∃ (n : Nat) (pend : Array PendingCheck) (s'' : AState),
    41      installFold mode pins (0, mkIFEnv IEnv.empty, #[]) ds.toList s = .ok (.ok (n, fe, pend), s') ∧
    42      checkPendingList mode fe pend.toList s'.worker = .ok (.ok (), s'')

== ConAgua/Final/Twin.lean#L116-L132
   116  /-- **What the twin's accept means, in con-leche's terms**: con-leche's parser reads the chunks, and
   117  con-leche's pure fold accepts the parsed records prepared with some prelude, at the twin's pin
   118  list. `stages_frame`, then Theorem 1 (`Arena.pooledAccepts_bridge`, with its two tier specs
   119  discharged by `CoreSpec.of_core` and `indSpec_of_bridge`). -/
   120  theorem twinAccepts_pure {chunks : List ByteArray} (h : TwinAccepts chunks) :
   121      ∃ (pins : List NatOpPinSet) (preC : ConLeche.Frontend.PreludeIx)
   122        (rc : ConLeche.Frontend.ParseResultD) (F : Nat) (env : Env),
   123        ConLeche.Frontend.parseChunks chunks = .ok rc ∧
   124        checkDeclsPure .verified (fueledOps .verified F) pins
   125          (ConLeche.Frontend.preparePrelude preC rc.decls).toList = .ok env := by
   126    obtain ⟨pins, sA, sB, sC, sD, sE, sF, pre, r, ds, ipins, fe, hA, hB, hC, hD, hE, hF⟩ := h
   127    have hk : CoreSpec .verified ConRon.Arena.checkFuel := CoreSpec.of_core rfl
   128    have hind : IndSpec .verified := ConRon.Bridge.Inductives.indSpec_of_bridge rfl hk
   129    obtain ⟨-, hfold, hipins, hpps, hpd, preC, rc, hrc, hden⟩ := stages_frame hA hB hC hD hE
   130    obtain ⟨env, F, -, hpure⟩ :=
   131      ConRon.Bridge.Arena.pooledAccepts_bridge rfl hk hind hpps hfold hipins hpd hden (pooledAccepts_of_seq hF)
   132    exact ⟨pins, preC, rc, F, env, hrc, hpure⟩

== ConAgua/Final/Statement.lean#L120-L127
   120  /-- **The caller's registers are intact on return**, relative to the registers `r0` at the call:
   121  `rsp` is past the return address and the other callee-saved registers of System V, `rbp`,
   122  `r14`, `r15`, `rbx`, `r12`, `r13`, hold their values from the call. The trampoline `ca_enter`
   123  saves and restores them (`rbp`, `r14` on the machine stack, the others past the table), so this
   124  holds whatever registers the compiled code uses. Together with the verdict in `rdx`/`rax` this is
   125  all the harness relies on after the call. -/
   126  def RegsRestored (r0 r : Reg64s) : Prop :=
   127    r.rsp.toNat = r0.rsp.toNat + 8 ∧ r.rbp = r0.rbp ∧ r.r14 = r0.r14 ∧ r.r15 = r0.r15 ∧

== ConAgua/Final/Abi.lean#L21-L47
    21  /-- **How the harness calls `ca_start`**: System V arguments `rdi, rsi` = the input buffer and its
    22  length, `rdx, rcx` = the pin-data buffer and its length, `r8, r9` = the region and its length;
    23  the buffers hold `b` and `pb`; the region is zero, in the address space, and apart from both
    24  buffers; the buffers are apart from each other; the return address is on the machine stack, whose
    25  32 bytes around `rsp` are mapped and apart from the region and the buffers. -/
    26  structure AbiCall (b pb : ByteArray) (dm : MachineData) (ra : Word) : Prop where
    27    hin : ∀ i (h : i < b.size), dm.dmem.get? (A (dm.regs.rdi.toNat + i)) = some b[i]
    28    hn : dm.regs.rsi.toNat = b.size
    29    hpins : ∀ i (h : i < pb.size), dm.dmem.get? (A (dm.regs.rdx.toNat + i)) = some pb[i]
    30    hnp : dm.regs.rcx.toNat = pb.size
    31    hzero : ∀ x, dm.regs.r8.toNat ≤ x → x < dm.regs.r8.toNat + dm.regs.r9.toNat → dm.dmem.get? (A x) = some 0
    32    hfits : dm.regs.r8.toNat + dm.regs.r9.toNat < 2 ^ 64
    33    hinEnd : dm.regs.rdi.toNat + b.size < 2 ^ 64
    34    hpinsEnd : dm.regs.rdx.toNat + pb.size < 2 ^ 64
    35    hinDisj : ∀ x, dm.regs.rdi.toNat ≤ x → x < dm.regs.rdi.toNat + b.size →
    36      x < dm.regs.r8.toNat ∨ dm.regs.r8.toNat + dm.regs.r9.toNat ≤ x
    37    hpinsDisj : ∀ x, dm.regs.rdx.toNat ≤ x → x < dm.regs.rdx.toNat + pb.size →
    38      x < dm.regs.r8.toNat ∨ dm.regs.r8.toNat + dm.regs.r9.toNat ≤ x
    39    hbufDisj : ∀ x, dm.regs.rdi.toNat ≤ x → x < dm.regs.rdi.toNat + b.size →
    40      ¬ (dm.regs.rdx.toNat ≤ x ∧ x < dm.regs.rdx.toNat + pb.size)
    41    hra : rdW dm.dmem (A dm.regs.rsp.toNat) = some ra
    42    hcs : ∀ x, dm.regs.rsp.toNat - 24 ≤ x → x < dm.regs.rsp.toNat + 8 →
    43      (dm.dmem.get? (A x)).isSome ∧ (x < dm.regs.r8.toNat ∨ dm.regs.r8.toNat + dm.regs.r9.toNat ≤ x) ∧
    44      ¬ (dm.regs.rdi.toNat ≤ x ∧ x < dm.regs.rdi.toNat + b.size) ∧
    45      ¬ (dm.regs.rdx.toNat ≤ x ∧ x < dm.regs.rdx.toNat + pb.size)
    46    hcs24 : 24 ≤ dm.regs.rsp.toNat
    47    hcs8 : dm.regs.rsp.toNat + 8 < 2 ^ 64

== ConAgua/Final/Twin.lean#L24-L26
    24  The prelude is free: `builtinPreludeE_run` gives *some* con-leche prelude `preC` the twin's prelude
    25  denotes, and con-leche's `preparePrelude` puts its records into the checked stream, so soundness
    26  holds whatever the prelude bytes are. The pins are free for the same reason as in con-leche.

== ConAgua/Checker/Pipeline.lean#L66-L69
    66  /-- What every stage may assume of the inputs: a 64-bit platform, both buffers below `2^63`
    67  bytes, every word array below `2^64` words. -/
    68  def InputsOK (b pb : ByteArray) (s64 : List Nat) : Prop :=
    69    System.Platform.numBits = 64 ∧ b.size < 2 ^ 63 ∧ pb.size < 2 ^ 63 ∧ ∀ n ∈ s64, n < 2 ^ 64

== scripts/check-asm.sh#L1-L12
     1  #!/usr/bin/env bash
     2  # Assemble and disassemble every program the compiler proof covers (the scanner, the `lit` store,
     3  # the arena walk, and the whole checker: the committed file `checker.s`, whose code the final
     4  # theorems are about, docs/design/asmfile.md) and check, instruction by instruction, that what `as`/`objdump` actually encode
     5  # agrees with what `asmText` (Kraken's AT&T printer) printed. This is the trusted-base check: the
     6  # printer and the assembler are *not* proved, so
     7  # `compile_correct` only holds of the real machine if their printed/assembled text means what
     8  # Kraken's instruction semantics says, and this is as close to checking that automatically as we
     9  # get. See DESIGN.md ("the compiler", lane `walk`) and docs/gaps/kraken-att-imul-three-operand.lean
    10  # (the mismatch this script would have caught before it was found by hand).
    11  #
    12  # Usage: scripts/check-asm.sh (from anywhere in the repo; rebuilds the emitters it needs).

== main.c#L97-L127
    97  /* Read `path` whole: read(2) until end of file into a malloc'd buffer that grows by doubling.
    98     The bytes `b` the theorem talks about are whatever this buffer holds. Fails on a read error and
    99     on 2^63 bytes or more (`AbiCall`'s `b.size < 2^63`). */
   100  static uint8_t *slurp(const char *path, uint64_t *n) {
   101    int fd = open(path, O_RDONLY);
   102    if (fd < 0) fail(path, strerror(errno));
   103    /* start with room for a regular file's size plus one, so that the read which sees end of file
   104       needs no growth (and a big input is never copied by realloc) */
   105    struct stat st;
   106    size_t cap = fstat(fd, &st) == 0 && st.st_size > 0 ? (size_t)st.st_size + 1 : 1 << 16;
   107    size_t len = 0;
   108    uint8_t *buf = malloc(cap);
   109    if (!buf) fail(path, strerror(errno));
   110    for (;;) {
   111      if (len == cap) {
   112        if (cap > SIZE_MAX / 2) fail(path, "too large");
   113        cap *= 2;
   114        buf = realloc(buf, cap);
   115        if (!buf) fail(path, strerror(errno));
   116      }
   117      ssize_t k = read(fd, buf + len, cap - len);
   118      if (k < 0 && errno == EINTR) continue;
   119      if (k < 0) fail(path, strerror(errno));
   120      if (k == 0) break;
   121      len += (size_t)k;
   122    }
   123    close(fd);
   124    if ((uint64_t)len >= 1ull << 63) fail(path, "too large");
   125    *n = len;
   126    return buf;
   127  }

== ConAgua/Final/ThreadsFinal.lean#L124-L148
   124  /-- **What the threaded harness does** (trusted; the module doc lists it): entry 1 at `dm₀`
   125  returning at `st₀`, the buffer `B`, and the threads `ths`. -/
   126  structure ThreadsRun [Host] (b pb : ByteArray) (dm₀ : MachineData) (ra₀ : Word) (st₀ : MachineState)
   127      (B : Array Word) (ths : List ThreadM) : Prop where
   128    call₀ : AbiCall b pb dm₀ ra₀
   129    ret₀ : FirstReturn dm₀ (label abiStartAL) ra₀ st₀
   130    rdx₀ : st₀.data.regs.rdx = 0
   131    rax₀ : 9223372036854775808 ≤ st₀.data.regs.rax.toNat
   132    /-- the buffer: `OUT`'s first `len` words, `len` its word `1` -/
   133    bufw : ∀ i (h : i < B.size), rdW st₀.data.dmem (A (outAddr dm₀.regs.r8.toNat + 8 * i)) = some B[i]
   134    buflen : ∃ w, rdW st₀.data.dmem (A (outAddr dm₀.regs.r8.toNat + 8)) = some w ∧ w.toNat = B.size
   135    /-- the calls: the buffer in place, each thread on its region -/
   136    calls : ∀ t ∈ ths, ∀ i < t.n, BufCallH B (t.dm i) (t.ra i) ∧
   137      (t.dm i).regs.rdi.toNat = outAddr dm₀.regs.r8.toNat ∧ (t.dm i).regs.rcx.toNat = t.base ∧
   138      (t.dm i).regs.r8.toNat = t.blen
   139    zero : ∀ t ∈ ths, 0 < t.n → ∀ x, t.base ≤ x → x < t.base + t.blen → (t.dm 0).dmem.get? (A x) = some 0
   140    ret : ∀ t ∈ ths, ∀ i < t.n, FirstReturn (t.dm i) (label abiCheckBL) (t.ra i) (t.st i)
   141    acc : ∀ t ∈ ths, ∀ i < t.n, (t.st i).data.regs.rdx = 0 ∧ (t.st i).data.regs.rax = ACCEPT
   142    /-- route A: the buffer's words at each call's return -/
   143    kept : ∀ t ∈ ths, ∀ i < t.n, ∀ q (h : q < B.size),
   144      rdW (t.st i).data.dmem (A (outAddr dm₀.regs.r8.toNat + 8 * q)) = some B[q]
   145    next : ∀ t ∈ ths, ∀ i, i + 1 < t.n → ∀ x, t.base ≤ x → x < t.base + t.blen →
   146      (t.dm (i + 1)).dmem.get? (A x) = (t.st i).data.dmem.get? (A x)
   147    claimed : ∀ t ∈ ths, ∀ i < t.n, (t.dm i).regs.rdx < st₀.data.regs.rax - 9223372036854775808
   148    cover : ∀ j : Word, j < st₀.data.regs.rax - 9223372036854775808 → ∃ t ∈ ths, ∃ i < t.n, (t.dm i).regs.rdx = j

== ConAgua/Final/ThreadsFinal.lean#L15-L34
    15  **What the theorem trusts of the harness** (the hypotheses of `ThreadsRun`; beyond them, what
    16  `Final/Statement.lean` lists: Kraken's semantics, the assembler, linker and loader):
    17  
    18  * **Entry 1's call**: `ca_start_a` is called as `AbiCall` says (the input and pin buffers, a zero
    19    region, the 32 bytes of machine stack around `rsp`; `mmap` gives the stated memory facts).
    20  * **First return** (`FirstReturn`): the harness regains control, at each call's return address,
    21    in a state that has every property the machine is guaranteed to reach at that address
    22    (`abiA_outcome`'s and `abiB_outcome`'s posts).
    23  * **The buffer** is the first `len` words of `OUT`'s slot of entry 1's region at its return, `len`
    24    `OUT`'s word `1`, and stays in place: every thread's call is passed its address and sees the
    25    same words, before the call and at its return (**route A**: read-only, `mprotect`).
    26  * **Each thread's region** is its own (pthreads: the threads' regions are apart from each other,
    27    from the buffer and from every thread's stack window): zero at the thread's first call, and at
    28    each later call holding the bytes the previous call left. Each call is made as `BufCallH` says
    29    (the region mapped and large enough, the buffer apart from it, the return address and the
    30    32-byte stack window).
    31  * **The claim counter's coverage**: every claimed group index `j` (in `rdx`) is below `k`
    32    (`k = rax - 2^63` from entry 1), and every index below `k` is claimed by some thread.
    33  * The verdicts: entry 1 returns `rdx = 0`, `rax ≥ 2^63`; every call returns `rdx = 0`,
    34    `rax = ACCEPT`.

== ConAgua/Compiler/Main.lean#L24-L28
    24  /-- What the harness sees after `ca_enter` returns, against L's result. -/
    25  def OutcomeRel (G : Layout) : Except Err (List Word × Mem) → MachineData → Prop
    26    | .ok (rs, m'), s => s.regs.rdx = 0 ∧ ResOut G G.tab.nres rs s ∧ MemRel G m' s.dmem
    27    | .error .outOfFuel, _ => False
    28    | .error _, s => s.regs.rdx = 2

== ConAgua/L/Syntax.lean#L5-L15
     5  /-!
     6  # L: abstract syntax
     7  
     8  L is the small first-order language the checker is written in (see `DESIGN.md`, "The language L").
     9  Values are 64-bit words with wrapping arithmetic. A function has numbered locals, the first
    10  `nparams` of which are its parameters. Memory is a fixed set of arrays: byte arrays (the input
    11  buffer) and word arrays, each named by a static index, and a store of global word variables
    12  (`GVar`), also named by static indices. Expressions have no side effects and
    13  make no calls; a call is a statement. Conditions are a separate type, with short-circuit `&&`/`||`
    14  so that a guard such as `i < len && b[i] == c` cannot read out of bounds.
    15  -/

== ConAgua/Compiler/Main.lean#L727-L750
   727  /-- **The end-to-end compiler theorem** (`compile_correct_frame` without the memory frame): the
   728  caller's `rsp`, `rbp`, `r14`, `r15`, `rbx`, `r12`, `r13` are restored on every path, whatever
   729  registers the compiled functions use. -/

   731      (hwf : Prog.wf G.tab p = true) (k0 : Nat) (hcode : Code (compileProg G.tab p entry) k0)

   736      (hmem : MemRel G m d.dmem) (hroom : G.lo + 8 ≤ G.hi)
   737      (htop : rdW d.dmem (A G.T) = some (UInt64.ofNat G.hi))
   738      (hargv : ∀ i (h : i < args.length), rdW d.dmem (A (G.T + G.tab.args.toNat + 8 * i)) = some args[i])
   739      (hra : rdW d.dmem (A d.regs.rsp.toNat) = some ra)
   740      (hcs : ∀ x, d.regs.rsp.toNat - 24 ≤ x → x < d.regs.rsp.toNat + 8 →
   741        (d.dmem.get? (A x)).isSome ∧ ¬ G.InStack x ∧ ¬ G.InArr x ∧ ¬ G.InTab x)
   742      (hcs24 : 24 ≤ d.regs.rsp.toNat) (hcs8 : d.regs.rsp.toNat + 8 < 2 ^ 64)
   743      (hsv : ∀ x, G.tabEnd ≤ x → x < G.tabEnd + 32 → (d.dmem.get? (A x)).isSome ∧ ¬ G.InStack x ∧
   744        ¬ G.InArr x ∧ (x < d.regs.rsp.toNat - 24 ∨ d.regs.rsp.toNat + 8 ≤ x))

   747          st.data.regs.rbp = d.regs.rbp ∧ st.data.regs.r14 = d.regs.r14 ∧ st.data.regs.r15 = d.regs.r15 ∧
   748          CalleeKept d.regs st.data.regs ∧
   749          (st.data.regs.rdx = 1 ∨ OutcomeRel G (run p N entry args m) st.data))
   750        d (label enterL) :=

== ConAgua/Arena/IndIface.lean#L310-L321
   310  /-- **A refinement of the twin's `op` by the L call `f(args)`**: from any memory satisfying `pre`
   311  against `a₀`, a returning run keeps the caller's locals, the twin's run succeeds, and `post`
   312  relates the memories before and after, the twin's state after, the L results and the twin's
   313  result. Every stub spec and every refinement of the stage has this shape. -/
   314  def RefAM {α : Type} [Inhabited α] (p : Prog) (f : FnName) (args : List Word)
   315      (pre : Mem → AState → Prop) (op : AM α)
   316      (post : Mem → Mem → AState → List Word → α → Prop) : Prop :=
   317    ∀ (n : Nat) (s₀ : St) (a₀ : AState), pre s₀.mem a₀ →
   318      ⦃fun s => s = s₀⦄ invoke p (exec p n) f args
   319      ⦃fun r s' => LocEq s' s₀ ∧ AM.ok op a₀ ∧
   320        post s₀.mem s'.mem (AM.st op a₀) r (AM.res op a₀); ⊤⦄
   321

== vendor/con-ron/ConRon/Arena/Main.lean#L154-L190
   154  def runPipelineHead :
   155      AM (Except (CheckError × Nat) (Frontend.PreludeIx × Frontend.StateD)) := do
   156    -- **The reserved-name pins, interned ONCE** (task #97-P6-4a): immediately
   157    -- after the state is made and before the prelude, so the scratch tier is
   158    -- closed and every pinned handle is persistent.
   159    internReservedPins
   160    match ← Frontend.builtinPreludeE with
   161    | .error e => pure (.error e)
   162    | .ok pre => pure (.ok (pre, ← Frontend.StateD.init))
   163  
   164  /-- con-leche: ConLeche/Driver/Run.lean:236-424 checkMain
   165  The pipeline AFTER the parse: `preparePrelude`, then **the fold** (task
   166  #97d), then the verdict number.  Shared verbatim by the pure seam and by the
   167  driver's interleaved loop, which is what makes the two the same computation.
   168  
   169  The verdict number is con-leche's own, "a property of the INPUT"
   170  (`ConLeche/Driver/Run.lean`'s `checkMain`): the records the parse produced, which no later step
   171  moves.  The fold's own environment is discarded — an accept is the
   172  statement, not the environment.
   173  
   174  `internAllPins` runs BEFORE the fold and while the scratch tier is still off,
   175  which is what DESIGN §8.6 P2d means by "at startup": every pinned datum is in
   176  the persistent cons table before any declaration's check can intern one into
   177  a tier that is about to vanish. -/
   178  def runPipelineTail (mode : CheckMode) (pins : List NatOpPinSet)
   179      (pre : Frontend.PreludeIx) (r : Frontend.ParseResultD) :
   180      AM (Except CheckError Nat) := do
   181    -- The verdict number is read HERE, before the fold, so that `r` dies at
   182    -- `preparePrelude` instead of being pinned across the whole check (DESIGN
   183    -- §8.4: decide the rare branch, and read what a later line needs, BEFORE
   184    -- the expensive step).
   185    let records := r.decls.size
   186    let ds ← Frontend.preparePrelude pre r.decls
   187    let ipins ← internAllPins pins
   188    match ← installThenCheck mode ipins ds with
   189    | .error (e, n) => pure (.error (atDecl e n))
   190    | .ok _ => pure (.ok records)

== ConAgua/L/Syntax.lean#L69-L95
    69  /-- Word expressions. Reading an array can fail (out of bounds); nothing else can. -/
    70  inductive Expr where
    71    | const (w : Word)
    72    | var (x : Var)
    73    | bin (op : BinOp) (a b : Expr)
    74    /-- Byte `i` of byte array `a`, zero-extended. -/
    75    | ld8 (a : ArrId) (i : Expr)
    76    /-- Word `i` of word array `a`. -/
    77    | ld64 (a : ArrId) (i : Expr)
    78    /-- The length (in elements) of byte array `a`. -/
    79    | len8 (a : ArrId)
    80    /-- The length (in elements) of word array `a`. -/
    81    | len64 (a : ArrId)
    82    /-- A comparison as a word: `1` if it holds, else `0`. -/
    83    | cmpw (c : Cmp) (a b : Expr)
    84    /-- Byte `i` of the constant byte string `d` (read-only data, part of the program). -/
    85    | ldc (d : List UInt8) (i : Expr)
    86    /-- The global variable `g`. -/
    87    | glob (g : GVar)
    88    /-- Word `i` of tier `t` of the tiered array `a`: word array `tierA a t` (`a` for `t & 1 = 0`,
    89    `a + tierOff` for `t & 1 = 1`; lane tierarr, docs/design/tierarr.md). -/
    90    | ld64t (a : ArrId) (t i : Expr)
    91    /-- The length of tier `t` of the tiered array `a`. -/
    92    | len64t (a : ArrId) (t : Expr)
    93    /-- The little-endian word of the bytes `i, …, i + 7` of `s` (lane blkcopy). -/
    94    | ld8x8 (s : BSrc) (i : Expr)
    95    deriving Repr, DecidableEq, Inhabited

== ConAgua/L/Syntax.lean#L117-L151
   117  /-- Statements. -/
   118  inductive Stmt where
   119    | skip
   120    /-- `x := e` -/
   121    | set (x : Var) (e : Expr)
   122    /-- `a.u8[i] := e` (the low byte of `e`) -/
   123    | st8 (a : ArrId) (i e : Expr)
   124    /-- `a.u64[i] := e` -/
   125    | st64 (a : ArrId) (i e : Expr)
   126    | seq (s t : Stmt)
   127    | ite (c : Cond) (s t : Stmt)
   128    /-- `while c { s }`. Each iteration costs one unit of fuel. -/
   129    | while (c : Cond) (s : Stmt)
   130    /-- Leave the innermost loop. -/
   131    | brk
   132    /-- Return from the function with the values `es` (usually one). -/
   133    | ret (es : List Expr)
   134    /-- `(x₀, x₁, …) := f(args)`: `xᵢ` gets the callee's `i`-th result, `0` if it returned fewer.
   135    A call costs one unit of fuel. -/
   136    | call (xs : List Var) (f : FnName) (args : List Expr)
   137    /-- Stop the whole program with an error (Rust's `panic!`, an overflow check, …). -/
   138    | abort
   139    /-- `g := e` for a global variable `g`. -/
   140    | gset (g : GVar) (e : Expr)
   141    /-- `a⟨t⟩.u64[i] := e`: word `i` of tier `t` of the tiered array `a`. -/
   142    | st64t (a : ArrId) (t i e : Expr)
   143    /-- `copy D[di ..] := S[si ..] for n`: words `si, …, si + n - 1` of `S` to `di, …` of `D`, in
   144    ascending order; bounds checked once, before anything is written (lane blkcopy). -/
   145    | copy64 (d : WArr) (di : Expr) (s : WArr) (si n : Expr)
   146    /-- `copy D[di ..] := S.u8[si ..] for n`: the bytes zero-extended into words. -/
   147    | copy8w (d : WArr) (di : Expr) (s : BSrc) (si n : Expr)
   148    /-- `x := scan S.u8[i .. e] until c`: the first `j` in `[i, e)` with `c[S[j]] ≠ 0`, else `e`
   149    (`c`: a 256-byte class table, constant data). -/
   150    | scan8 (x : Var) (s : BSrc) (i e : Expr) (c : List UInt8)
   151    deriving Repr, Inhabited

== ConAgua/L/Syntax.lean#L153-L163
   153  /-- A function: `nparams` parameters, `nlocals ≥ nparams` locals (params first, the rest start
   154  at `0`), and a body. Falling off the end of the body (or a `break` outside a loop) returns no
   155  values (so every result the caller reads is `0`). -/
   156  structure FunDecl where
   157    nparams : Nat
   158    nlocals : Nat
   159    body : Stmt
   160    deriving Repr, Inhabited
   161  
   162  /-- A program: its functions, by name. The first binding of a name wins. -/
   163  abbrev Prog := List (FnName × FunDecl)

== ConAgua/L/Notation.lean#L385-L386

== ConAgua/L/Notation.lean#L10-L61
    10  # L: concrete syntax
    11  
    12  A Rust-like surface for writing L functions by hand:
    13  
    14  ```
    15  lfn (b_dummy, j) locals (c) {
    16    while j < len(IN.u8) {
    17      c := IN.u8[j];
    18      if c == '"' { return j } else { j += 1 }
    19    };
    20    return 0
    21  }
    22  ```
    23  
    24  * `lfn (params) locals (more) { body }` is a term of type `L.FunDecl`. Variable names resolve to
    25    local indices in declaration order (parameters first).
    26  * `A.u8[i]` / `A.u64[i]` read byte / word array `A`, where `A` is a Lean constant of type
    27    `L.ArrId`; `len(A.u8)` / `len(A.u64)` are the lengths. Stores are `A.u8[i] := e`.
    28  * `R[i].f` reads field `f` of record `i` of the record layout `R : L.Record` (a Lean constant;
    29    the field is the constant `R.f : L.Field`), `R[i].f := e` writes it: the word
    30    `i * stride + f.off` of the word array `R.arr` (`L/Records.lean`).
    31  * `A⟨t⟩[i]` reads word `i` of tier `t` of the tiered word array `A` (`L.tierA A t`: `A`, or
    32    `A + tierOff` when `t & 1 = 1`); `len(A⟨t⟩)` is that tier's length, `A⟨t⟩[i] := e` writes it,
    33    and `R⟨t⟩[i].f` / `R⟨t⟩[i].f := e` are records in a tiered array (lane tierarr).
    34  * The node stores' records (`L/TRec.lean`, the stores in `Arena/StoreFields.lean`; lane tieracc):
    35    `R⟨t, i⟩.f` is field `f` of node `i` of tier `t` of the store `R : L.TRec` (`R⟨t, i⟩` a one-word
    36    column), `R⟦h⟧.f` / `R⟦h⟧` the node the handle word `h` names, `R⟨t⟩.count` the node count of
    37    tier `t`, `⟦h⟧.tier` / `⟦h⟧.idx` a handle's tier bit and index; `R⟨t, i⟩.f := e` writes a field
    38    (the store library only).
    39  * `⦃x⦄.tier`, `⦃x⦄.idx`, `⦃x⦄.base` are the tier (bit 40), the index (the low 40 bits) and the
    40    tier's base address (`(x >> 40) << 40`) of a tier-tagged address `x`, and `A⦃x⦄` reads the word
    41    at the tagged address `x` of the tiered word array `A` (`A⟨⦃x⦄.tier⟩[⦃x⦄.idx]`). The limb
    42    pool's slices are named by such addresses: the tier is `1` for a slice of the scratch tier (open
    43    while the arena's scratch flag is set) and `0` otherwise (lane tierpool, docs/design/tierpool.md). A
    44    store's tier must be simple, so a writer decodes the tier and base of its top once into locals
    45    and indexes relative to the base: `t := ⦃top⦄.tier; b := ⦃top⦄.base; … A⟨t⟩[top + j - b] := e`
    46    (for a tier-0 top this is exactly `A[top + j]`, out-of-bounds aborts included). This macro is
    47    the one place that fixes the encoding.
    48  * `D.c8[i]` reads byte `i` of the constant byte string `D : List UInt8` (a Lean constant);
    49    `len(D.c8)` is its length (a constant).
    50  * Literals: numbers, characters (`'{'` is `123`), and `⟪t⟫` for any Lean term of type `Word`.
    51  * An identifier that is not a local names a global variable: a Lean constant `g : L.GVar`
    52    (`abbrev HTOP : L.GVar := ⟨3⟩`). `g` reads it, `g := e`, `g += e`, `g -= e` write it.
    53  * Operators `+ - * & | ^ << >>` (wrapping, as in Rust's `wrapping_*`), `mulhi(a, b)` (the high
    54    word of the 128-bit product), `u64(a < b)` (a comparison as `1`/`0`, Rust's `(a < b) as u64`),
    55    comparisons
    56    `== != < <= > >=` (unsigned) and `<ₛ ≤ₛ` (signed), and short-circuit `&& || !`.
    57  * Statements are separated by `;`: `x := e`, `x += e`, `x -= e`, `x := call f(e, …)`,
    58    `(x, y, …) := call f(e, …)` (several results), `if c { … } else { … }` (with `else if`),
    59    `while c { … }`, `break`, `return e`, `return (e, e', …)`, `abort`, `skip`, and `⟪t⟫` for a
    60    named block `t : L.Stmt` (see `lblk`; a block written with other variables than a prefix of
    61    the enclosing ones is an error).

== ConAgua/L/Semantics.lean#L7-L21
     7  /-!
     8  # L: semantics
     9  
    10  The meaning of an L program is a Lean function into the monad `M := StateT St (Except Err)`.
    11  It is executable (`#eval`), and it is what `vcgen` steps through in a proof.
    12  
    13  * `St` is the memory (`Mem`: the byte arrays and the word arrays) plus the current frame's locals.
    14  * `Err` is every way a run can fail. None of them is a result: a result is a list of words
    15    returned by the function, so "ran out of fuel" or "read out of bounds" can never read as "accept".
    16  * Fuel. `exec p n` is the `n`-th Kleene iterate of the one-step interpreter `step p`:
    17    `exec p 0` throws `outOfFuel`, and `exec p (n+1) = step p (exec p n)`. `step p k` interprets a
    18    statement by structural recursion and hands the next loop iteration and every callee body to
    19    `k`. So fuel bounds the nesting of loop iterations and calls along a path. A partial-correctness
    20    triple (exception post `⊤`) is proved by induction on `n` and never mentions fuel.
    21  -/

== ConAgua/L/Semantics.lean#L45-L55
    45  /-- The ways a run can fail. -/
    46  inductive Err where
    47    /-- The fuel (nesting of loop iterations and calls) ran out. -/
    48    | outOfFuel
    49    /-- An array access out of bounds, or to an array that does not exist. -/
    50    | oob
    51    /-- A call to an undefined function. -/
    52    | noFun (f : FnName)
    53    /-- An `abort` statement. -/
    54    | abort
    55    deriving Repr, DecidableEq, Inhabited

== ConAgua/L/Semantics.lean#L345-L352
   345  /-- The interpreter with `n` units of fuel. -/
   346  def exec (p : Prog) : Nat → Stmt → M Sig
   347    | 0, _ => throw .outOfFuel
   348    | n + 1, s => step p (exec p n) s
   349  
   350  /-- Run function `f` of `p` on memory `m`: its results and the final memory. -/
   351  def run (p : Prog) (fuel : Nat) (f : FnName) (vs : List Word) (m : Mem) : Except Err (List Word × Mem) :=
   352    ((invoke p (exec p fuel) f vs).run { mem := m, loc := Locals.init [] }).map fun (r, s) => (r, s.mem)

== ConAgua/L/Semantics.lean#L25-L32
    25  /-- The memory: a fixed set of byte arrays and word arrays, indexed by `ArrId`, and the global
    26  variables. The arrays' lengths are fixed for the run (a growable vector is a fixed-capacity array
    27  plus a length kept in a word). Every global variable has a value (`0` unless written). -/
    28  structure Mem where
    29    bytes : Array (Array UInt8) := #[]
    30    words : Array (Array Word) := #[]
    31    glob : GVar → Word := fun _ => 0
    32    deriving Inhabited

== ConAgua/L/Syntax.lean#L28-L35
    28  /-- **Tiered arrays** (lane tierarr). Tier `1` of word array `a` is word array `a + tierOff`;
    29  an access with a run-time tier word `t` uses `tierA a t` (the tier is masked: `t & 1`). So a
    30  program sees one array per tier, as con-ron's per-tier tables, and the compiler finds tier `1`'s
    31  descriptor at a fixed distance from tier `0`'s. -/
    32  @[expose] def tierOff : Nat := 256
    33  
    34  /-- The array of tier `t` of the tiered array `a`. -/
    35  @[expose] def tierA (a : ArrId) (t : UInt64) : ArrId := a + tierOff * (t &&& 1).toNat

== ConAgua/L/TRec.lean#L7-L31
     7  /-!
     8  # Tiered store records (surface syntax)
     9  
    10  A node store of the arena (`Arena/StoreFields.lean` lists them) keeps, per tier, an array of
    11  records of `w` words, and the node count of each tier in a control word. Code outside the store
    12  library reaches them only through the accessors below, written in L as
    13  
    14  * `R⟨t, i⟩.f`: field `f` of node `i` of tier `t` (`R⟨t, i⟩` for a one-word column);
    15  * `R⟦h⟧.f`, `R⟦h⟧`: the same for the node a handle word `h` names (tier bit 27, index the low 27
    16    bits);
    17  * `R⟨t⟩.count`: the node count of tier `t`;
    18  * `R⟨t, i⟩.f := e`: a field store (the store library's pushes only).
    19  
    20  They expand (`Notation.lean`) to the builders `TRec.ld`, `TRec.st`, `TRec.cntE` of this file,
    21  which fix the **layout** in one place: one tiered word array per store (lane tierswitch; tier
    22  `t` of array `a` is array `L.tierA a t`, docs/design/tierarr.md), node `i` of tier `t` at
    23  `arr⟨t⟩[i * w ..]`, the count at `CTL[ca + t]`. Proofs see the named words `TRec.ad`, `tfld`, `tcnt`.
    24  
    25  **Packed records** (lane memlay, `hi ≠ 0`): field `0` and field `hi` (two handle words, below
    26  `2^32`) share word `0` of the record, field `0` in bits 0–31 and field `hi` in bits 32–63; the
    27  other fields `f` follow in words `1 ‥` (`f`, or `f - 1` above `hi`), whole. A field's word is
    28  `TRec.wd`, its address `TRec.ad`; a load extracts the half (`TRec.ex`: `x & 0xFFFFFFFF`,
    29  `x >> 32`). Records are written once, whole, by the store library's pushes (the combined word
    30  `f₀ | f_hi << 32`); `TRec.st` stores a whole word (unpacked fields only).
    31  -/

== ConAgua/L/Notation.lean#L96-L97
    96  /-- `le64!(A.u8, i)`: the little-endian word of the bytes `i … i + 7` (`D.c8` for constant bytes). -/
    97  syntax "le64!" "(" ident ", " lexpr ")" : lexpr

== ConAgua/L/Notation.lean#L144-L150
   144  /-- `x := scan!(A.u8, i, e, C)`: the first `j ∈ [i, e)` whose byte is in the class `C` (a Lean
   145  constant: a 256-byte table), else `e` (`D.c8` for constant bytes; lane blkcopy). -/
   146  syntax ident " := " "scan!" "(" ident ", " lexpr ", " lexpr ", " ident ")" : lstmt
   147  /-- `copy!(D, di, S, si, n)`: `D[di + j] := S[si + j]` for `j < n` (`S` a word array `B.u64` or bytes
   148  `B.u8`/`B.c8`; `D⟨t⟩`, `S⟨t⟩` for tiered word arrays; lane blkcopy). -/
   149  syntax "copy!" "(" ident (noWs "⟨" lexpr "⟩")? ", " lexpr ", " ident (noWs "⟨" lexpr "⟩")? ", " lexpr ", "
   150    lexpr ")" : lstmt

== ConAgua/L/Semantics.lean#L129-L148
   129  /-- The little-endian word of the bytes `k, …, k + 7` of `b` (as the machine's 8-byte load
   130  reads them: Kraken's `Nat.ofBytes`). -/
   131  def le64 (b : Array UInt8) (k : Nat) : Word :=
   132    UInt64.ofNat (((List.range 8).map fun j => b[k + j]!).foldr (fun x acc => acc * 256 + x.toNat) 0)
   133  
   134  /-- `D[di + j] := S[si + j]` for `j < n`, ascending (each word read after the writes before it). -/
   135  def Mem.copy64 (m : Mem) (d : ArrId) (di : Word) (s : ArrId) (si : Word) : Nat → Mem
   136    | 0 => m
   137    | n + 1 => (m.set64 d di ((m.arr64 s)[si.toNat]!)).copy64 d (di + 1) s (si + 1) n
   138  
   139  /-- `D[di + j] := b[si + j]` (zero-extended) for `j < n`, ascending. -/
   140  def Mem.copy8w (m : Mem) (d : ArrId) (di : Word) (b : Array UInt8) (si : Word) : Nat → Mem
   141    | 0 => m
   142    | n + 1 => (m.set64 d di (b[si.toNat]!).toUInt64).copy8w d (di + 1) b (si + 1) n
   143  
   144  /-- The first `j` in `[i, e)` with `c[b[j]] ≠ 0`, else `e` (for `i ≤ e`). -/
   145  def scanN (b : Array UInt8) (c : List UInt8) (i e : Nat) : Nat :=
   146    if i < e then (if c[(b[i]!).toNat]! ≠ 0 then i else scanN b c (i + 1) e) else i
   147  termination_by e - i
   148  

== ConAgua/Compiler/Compile.lean#L611-L622
   611  /-- `copy D[di ..] := S[si ..] for n`: the source checked and pointed at by `rcx`, the
   612  destination by `rdx`, the end of the source in temporary `0`, then 6 instructions per word. -/
   613  def copy64Code (ctx : Ctx) (path : Path) (d : WArr) (di : Expr) (s : WArr) (si n : Expr) : Program :=
   614    (warrDesc ctx .rcx s).1 ++ [movRM .rax (mb (warrDesc ctx .rcx s).2 (ctx.tab.len64 s.arr))] ++
   615    lenChk ctx si n ++ wordPtr ctx .rcx (warrDesc ctx .rcx s).2 s.arr si ++
   616    (warrDesc ctx .rdx d).1 ++ [movRM .rax (mb (warrDesc ctx .rdx d).2 (ctx.tab.len64 d.arr))] ++
   617    lenChk ctx di n ++ wordPtr ctx .rdx (warrDesc ctx .rdx d).2 d.arr di ++
   618    [i64 (.mov (.reg (rr .rax)) (opnd ctx n)),
   619     i64 (.shl (.reg (rr .rax)) (.imm8 (.int64 (Int64.ofInt 3)))),
   620     i64 (.add (.reg (rr .rax)) (oR .rcx)), movMR (ctx.tmp 0) .rax,
   621     i64 (.cmp (.reg (rr .rcx)) (oM (ctx.tmp 0))), jccL .nc (ctx.lbl path "X")] ++
   622    copy64Loop (ctx.lbl path "L") (ctx.tmp 0) ++ [.label (ctx.lbl path "X")]

== ConAgua/Compiler/Compile.lean#L644-L651
   644  /-- The loop of `scan8`: per byte the byte, its class (constant data at `[r15 + off]`) and the
   645  tests, 7 instructions. -/
   646  def scanLoop (Lb Xb : Label) (off : Int) (eo : Operand .W64) : Program :=
   647    [.label Lb,
   648     i64 (.movzx (.reg (rr .rdx)) (w' := .W8) (.mem (mbi .rcx .rax .W8))),
   649     i64 (.movzx (.reg (rr .rdx)) (w' := .W8) (.mem (tblAddr off))),
   650     i64 (.cmp (.reg (rr .rdx)) (oI 0)), jccL .nz Xb,
   651     i64 (.add (.reg (rr .rax)) (oI 1)), i64 (.cmp (.reg (rr .rax)) eo), jccL .c Lb]

== ConAgua/L/TRec.lean#L93-L97
    93  /-- The tier of a handle word: bit 27. -/
    94  @[expose] def tierE (h : Expr) : Expr := .bin .and (.bin .shr h (.const 27)) (.const 1)
    95  
    96  /-- The node index of a handle word: the low 27 bits. -/
    97  @[expose] def idxE (h : Expr) : Expr := .bin .and h (.const 134217727)

== ConAgua/Arena/StoreFields.lean#L9-L31
     9  # The store records: one accessor per field, one evaluation lemma per accessor (lane tieracc)
    10  
    11  Every node store of the arena keeps its records in a word array and its node counts in `CTL`
    12  (`L/TRec.lean`). This file is the **only** place outside the store library that knows the
    13  layout:
    14  
    15  * **The stores** (`LIT`, `APP`, …, `LVLS`) and their one-word columns (`APP_DER`, …, `FVAR_LP`), as
    16    `L.TRec` values, with a constant per field (`APP.f`, `APP.a`, …). L code reads them as
    17    `APP⟨t, i⟩.f`, `APP⟦h⟧.a`, `APP⟨t⟩.count` (`L/Notation.lean`).
    18  * **The proof accessors** `tfld m R t i f` (field `f` of node `i` of tier `t`) and `tcnt m R t`
    19    (the node count of tier `t`), and the handle decoders `tierW`, `idxW`.
    20  * **One evaluation lemma per accessor**: `evalE_tld` / `tld_eq` (pass both to `vcgen`, as
    21    `ld64`), `evalE_cnt` / `tcntM_eq`, `evalE_tierE`, `evalE_idxE`, and the pure forms
    22    `Expr.pval_tld`, `Expr.pval_cntE`, … (`lang_grind`); the frame lemmas `tfld_set64_ne`,
    23    `tcnt_set64_ne`, `tfld_setG`, ….
    24  
    25  Proofs outside the store library state models and relations with `tfld` and `tcnt` and never
    26  unfold them (`TRec.ad` stays folded). The layout (one tiered array per store, lane
    27  `tierswitch`: tier `t` of array `a` is `tierA a t`) lives in `L/TRec.lean`, the definitions and
    28  lemma proofs here, and the store library.
    29  
    30  The array and control-word ids below are the memory map's (`AREC` = `APP.arr`, …): each store
    31  file's `abbrev` must agree, `StoreFieldsCheck.lean` checks it.

== ConAgua/Arena/ConsLib.lean#L205-L214
   205  /-! ## The slot layout (KSTP)
   206  
   207  Each tier has its own slot array `sa⟨t⟩` (lane tierswitch; con-ron's per-tier tables). Its words
   208  `0` and `1` hold `n - SN0` (`n` the slot count, a multiple of 8) and `o`, the table's offset (`0`:
   209  nothing writes it); the table starts at word `r = 2 + o`. Slot `j` is the two words `r + 2 j` (the
   210  value: `0` free, `B t + i + 1` node `i`) and `r + 2 j + 1` (the key word). The table grows at load
   211  3/4 (con-ron's `HashMap2`) and **in place** (lane memlay): it doubles where it is (`kgrowB`), so no
   212  old copy of it stays resident, and the growth aborts if the array cannot hold the doubled table.
   213  A fresh array (all zero) is a table of `SN0` slots at offset `0`: a small run touches only the
   214  array's first words.

== ConAgua/Arena/ConsLib.lean#L485-L490
   485  /-- The growth test: the tier grows when its node count `c + 1` passes 3/4 of its slot count
   486  `g + SN0` (`(g + SN0) * 3 < (c + 1) * 4`; con-ron's `HashMap2` load factor `LOAD_NUM/LOAD_DEN`). -/
   487  def cpGrowIf (C : ConsSch) : Stmt :=
   488    .ite (.cmp .ult (.bin .mul (.bin .add (.var (gO C + 1)) (.const SN0)) (.const 3))
   489        (.bin .mul (.bin .add (.var (2 + C.np)) (.const 1)) (.const 4)))
   490      (kgrowBlk C) .skip

== ConAgua/Arena/ConsLib.lean#L462-L468
   462  /-- **The growth of tier `t`, in place** (con-ron's `HashMap2::try_resize` doubles into a new
   463  table and frees the old one; here the table doubles where it is, so no old copy stays resident):
   464  the slot count doubles, the new upper half is zeroed, every live slot of the old half is marked,
   465  then each marked entry is re-inserted from its home in the doubled table (linear probing past
   466  the live unmarked slots; a marked slot met on the way is swapped and re-inserted next: absl's
   467  in-place rehash). Aborts if the array cannot hold the doubled table. Template variables
   468  `t n2 n H Q ob nb x e v q h j d bt` (`t` the push's tier, the others from `gO`). -/

== ConAgua/Arena/SlotGrow.lean#L40-L43
    40  /-- The home slot of hash `h` among `n`: con-ron's multiply-xor finaliser, then the high word
    41  of the product with `n` (Lemire's range reduction) in place of the power-of-two mask. -/
    42  def homeW (h n : Word) : Word :=
    43    UInt64.ofNat (((h * golden) ^^^ ((h * golden) >>> 32)).toNat * n.toNat / 2 ^ 64)

== ConAgua/Arena/Scratch.lean#L10-L29
    10  /-!
    11  # The scratch tier's lifecycle in L: open and drop without zeroing a slot
    12  
    13  con-ron's arena brackets every declaration check with `enterScratch` (open the scratch tier of all
    14  four stores, clear the walk memos) and `dropScratch` (`flushCaches`, then close the scratch tier
    15  and truncate it). In L the 19 tables keep their scratch tier as tier 1 of their slot and record
    16  arrays (`StoreLib.lean`); a slot of tier 1 holds `B + i + 1` for node `i`, with the **slot base**
    17  `B = CTL[62]` (`SCB`), and reads free at or below `B` (`slotV`). So emptying the scratch tier of
    18  every table is O(1) per table:
    19  
    20  * `scratch_reset(f)`: `B += 2^32`, the scratch flag `CTL[1] := f`, and the 19 tier-1 node
    21    counts `CTL[ca + 1] := 0`. Every old scratch slot holds at most `B + 2^27` and reads free
    22    against the new base; no slot is written. Once every `2^30` resets (`B ≥ 2^62`) the base wraps:
    23    the 19 scratch slot tables are zeroed and `B` restarts at `0` (con-ron's `clear` at
    24    `EPOCH_MAX`), so `B < 2^62 + 2^32` always holds.
    25  * `scratch_enter()`: `scratch_reset(1)` and the four walk memos' `clear` (epoch bumps).
    26  * `scratch_drop()`: `flush_caches()` (`CoreCaches.lean`, the per-declaration caches), then
    27    `scratch_reset(0)`.
    28  
    29  The refinement (`enterScratch`/`dropScratch` under `ArenaD`) is `ScratchRefine.lean`.

== ConAgua/Arena/MemoLib.lean#L9-L36
     9  /-!
    10  # The memo library: per-call memo tables with two-word keys and epoch stamps
    11  
    12  con-ron's arena keeps six per-call memos keyed `(EIdx × Nat)` (`inst1C`, `instLC`, `liftC`,
    13  `abs1C`, `inst1LC`, `instLPC`), two keyed `EIdx` (`bvarBC`, `fvarBC`) and two level ones
    14  (`Arena/Monad.lean`'s `Memos`); con-ron's Rust keeps them in `HashMap2` (`ron/hashmap2.rs`): open
    15  addressing, linear probing, an **epoch stamp** per slot so that `clear` is `epoch += 1`.
    16  
    17  A memo here is a **schema** `MemoSch`: a word array `arr` and a `CTL` index `cs` (`CTL[cs]` is the
    18  live stamp minus one, `CTL[cs + 1]` the live count). Four words per slot: the stamp, the key's two
    19  words, the value. A one-word key (`bvarBC`) is the two-word key with second word `0`. Slot `j` is
    20  **live** iff its stamp is `CTL[cs] + 1`; anything else is free space, so all-zero memory is an
    21  empty memo.
    22  
    23  The L code is **generic in the schema**: `memoFindG S`, `memoPutG S`, `memoClearG S` are Lean
    24  functions producing L functions with the schema's array and `CTL` words spliced in (`S.arr.u64[…]`,
    25  `CTL.u64[⟪S.cs⟫]`), and their `vcgen` specs are proved once, for a variable schema. An instance is
    26  three entries of the program (`("bm_find", memoFindG bmSch)`, …) and no proof.
    27  
    28  * `X_find(k1, k2)`: the probe from `homeW (k1 ^ (k2 << 32) ^ (k2 >> 32) * golden)`, returning
    29    `(found, slot, steps)`. Both halves of `k2` enter the hash: banked memos (`MemoBank.genW`), the
    30    eager bit and `rrSch` keep a second component in `k2`'s high half (lane `rfhash`: with only
    31    `k2 << 32` it was shifted out, and all banks' entries for one `k1` shared one probe cluster).
    32  * `X_put(k1, k2, v, fd, j)`: given the probe's `fd`, `j` **on the current memory**, write the
    33    value (and on a miss, the stamp and the key, growing the table past 3/4 load, con-ron's `HashMap2` load factor). Callers probe right
    34    before (`set` = `find; put`); a walk that recursed since its first probe probes again.
    35  * `X_clear()`: `CTL[cs] += 1`, `CTL[cs + 1] := 0`, aborting where the stamp would wrap.
    36  -/

== ConAgua/Arena/Pool.lean#L8-L27
     8  /-!
     9  # The limb pool: layout, abstraction, invariant
    10  
    11  con-ron's `ron::Nat` (`crates/con-ron-core/src/ron/nat.rs`) is a `Vec<u64>` of little-endian
    12  limbs with no trailing zero limb. In L there are no vectors: every number lives in ONE word array,
    13  the limb pool `POOL`, as a slice `(o, l)` (offset, length). The pool grows at the top: word 0 of
    14  the control array `CTL` holds the top `T`; `[0, T)` is in use, `[T, len(POOL))` is free. A
    15  function that makes a number appends its limbs at `T` and moves `T` up; nothing below `T` is
    16  ever written again, so every slice handed out stays valid (the frame is `Agree`).
    17  
    18  * abstraction: `pv p o l` is the number the slice `(o, l)` of the pool array `p` denotes,
    19    `Σ_{i<l} p[o+i] * 2^(64 i)`;
    20  * normal form: `Norm p o l`: the slice has no trailing zero limb (con-ron's `Nat.WF`), so equal
    21    numbers have equal slices up to position;
    22  * invariant of the pool (`PoolOK`): `T ≤ len(POOL) < 2^64` and `CTL` has its word.
    23  
    24  All of this is stated over the pool *array* `p : Array Word` and Lean `Nat` positions, and the
    25  lemmas are guarded equations about the named functions `pv`, `xv`, `lv`, registered for
    26  `grind` with multi-patterns that bind every variable (DESIGN.md, "Proof recipe").
    27  -/

== ConAgua/Compiler/Abi.lean#L8-L32
     8  # The entry stubs (lane `abi`)
     9  
    10  The harness's whole job shrinks to: map a zero region, hand over the two input buffers, call
    11  `ca_start(in, in_len, pins, pins_len, base, base_len)` once. `ca_start` is the sequential driver
    12  (`parStub`, below): it calls entry 1 and then entry 2 on the same region. Both go through the
    13  setup stub `ca_setup` (`abiStub`, an internal label; the argument registers as `ca_start`'s),
    14  emitted before the trampoline, which sets up inside the region everything the harness used to lay
    15  out (`L.Compiler.Tab`), then tail-jumps into the trampoline `ca_enter(T, fuel)`:
    16  
    17  * System V arguments: `rdi`/`rsi` = the input bytes (byte array `0`), `rdx`/`rcx` = the pin-data
    18    bytes (byte array `1`; ignored if the program has one byte array), `r8` = `base`, `r9` =
    19    `base_len`. Returns `rax`/`rdx` as `ca_enter` does.
    20  * If `base_len < abiNeed`, it returns at once with `rdx = 1` (resources exhausted; never accept).
    21  * The region is a static partition into `abiSlot`-byte slots (no allocator; the pages that are
    22    never touched never become real): slot `0` is the table (`T = base`), slot `1` the L stack
    23    (`abiStack` bytes at its bottom), then one slot per byte array `2, …, nb - 1` and per word array.
    24    Each array starts at its slot's start; its length is `abiSlot` bytes, resp. `abiWords` words.
    25  * The constant data is written into the table by immediate stores (no `.rodata` read); the result
    26    area and the global variables are the region's zeros.
    27  * The fuel is `2^62 - 1` (`compile_correct` takes any `N < 2^62`).
    28  
    29  Nothing here is trusted: `sim_abiStub` (`ConAgua/Compiler/AbiSim.lean`) runs the stub on the
    30  machine, `abiLayout_ok` and `abi_memRel` (`ConAgua/Final/Abi.lean`) show that it establishes
    31  `Layout.Ok`/`MemRel` for the partition, and `abi_harness` gives `compile_correct`'s premises at
    32  the trampoline. -/

== ConAgua/Arena/LevelEquiv.lean#L249-L259

   250  fresh heap (the top reset to `0`). The verdict cache `lvlEqC` is `lvl_eq_c`'s, in front of this
   251  function (`CoreLevels.lean`); this is the uncached computation (`LevelArena.lean`,
   252  `lvlEq_refines`). -/
   253  -- con-ron: ConRon/Arena/Core.lean:132-149 ConRon.Arena.lvlEq?

   255  def lvlEqL : FunDecl := lfn (u, v) locals (z) {
   256    CTL.u64[192] := 0;
   257    z := call lv_equiv(u, v);
   258    return z
   259  }

== ConAgua/Arena/LevelEquiv.lean#L244-L247

   246    | 0, _, _, _ => none
   247    | n + 1, m, u, v => equivW n (m.set64 CTL 192 0) u v

== vendor/con-ron/ConRon/Arena/Core.lean#L132-L149
   132  /-- con-leche: ConLeche/Kernel/Level.lean:164-169 isEquiv — `Level.isEquiv`
   133  at two level HANDLES, with the verdict cached on the pair.  `none` is
   134  con-leche's fuel exhaustion and is never cached. -/
   135  def lvlEq? (u v : LIdx) : AM (Option Bool) := do
   136    let s ← get
   137    match s.caches.lvlEqC[(u, v)]? with
   138    | some r => pure (some r)
   139    | none => do
   140      let lu ← readLevelM u
   141      let lv ← readLevelM v
   142      match Level.isEquiv lu lv with
   143      | some r => do
   144        let s ← get
   145        let mp := s.caches.lvlEqC
   146        let s := { s with caches := { s.caches with lvlEqC := ∅ } }
   147        set { s with caches := { s.caches with lvlEqC := mp.insert (u, v) r } }
   148        pure (some r)
   149      | none => pure none

== ConAgua/L/ModelGen.lean#L9-L60
     9  /-!
    10  # Generated word models and specs (`l_model`)
    11  
    12  `l_model` reads the `lfn` text of a group of L functions and generates, for each function `f`,
    13  
    14  * its **word model** `fW : Nat → Mem → Word → … → Option (Word × Mem)` (`Option Word` for a
    15    read-only function, `ro`; no fuel argument for a single function that needs none): the L code
    16    with every local inlined, `abort` as `none`, a load as `rdW`, a store as `Mem.set64`, a call to a
    17    group member as that member's model at fuel `n`, a call to another function as the model its
    18    spec states (`specs`), and the code after an effectful call as a first-order continuation
    19    `fW.k_g` (`| none => none | some (x, m₁) => …`) over the locals it reads, named after the
    20    callee `g` (`fW.k_g_2`, … for its later calls, in source order; after a loop `fW.k_loopᵢ`), so
    21    that a change elsewhere in the code does not rename it. The code after an `if`
    22    whose branches both fall through is a join point `fW.jᵢ` over the locals and the memory (no
    23    copy of it). Equal continuations of the group are shared;
    24  * a function with **several results** (`return (a, b, …)`) gets a list model
    25    `Option (List Word × Mem)` (`return e` is `some ([e], m)`, the end of the body `some ([], m)`;
    26    `↦ fW list` forces it), or with `↦ fW tuple` a tuple model `Option (Word × … × Mem)` (the
    27    longest `return`'s arity, shorter ones padded with `0`);
    28  * a **loop** (`while c { … }` in the `lfn`, or a spliced named block `⟪X⟫` that is one `while`)
    29    is a model of its own, `fW.loopᵢ n m x₁ …` (`exec p n` on the loop: `| 0 => none | n + 1 =>
    30    if c then … fW.loopᵢ n … else exit`; the enclosing code applies it at `n + 1`), over the locals
    31    live at its head. Its result is `(signal, outs…, memory)`: the signal (`Sig.normal`,
    32    `Sig.ret vs`) if the body has a `return`, the locals it assigns that the code after it reads,
    33    the memory unless read-only; the code after it is a continuation of that result. A loop with a
    34    `return` followed by the function's last statement (`return …`, `abort`) is **fused**: its model
    35    returns the function's result. Its spec `fW.loopᵢ.spec` (`⦃s = s₀⦄ exec p n X ⦃…⦄`, by
    36    induction, the model is the loop's meaning) is generated, and a `while` written in the `lfn`
    37    becomes the named block `fW.loopᵢ.stmt` (with `fW.lfn_eq : F = lfn … ⟪fW.loopᵢ.stmt⟫ …`).
    38    Named blocks without a loop are inlined;
    39  * one **guarded equation** `fW.armᵢ` per non-`none` leaf of the `if` tree of each model, loop and
    40    continuation (the path's conditions as hypotheses, in order; on the negative side in their
    41    natural form: `a = b` for `¬ a ≠ b`, `a ≠ b` for `¬ a = b`, `p` for `¬ ¬ p`), each with a `grind_pattern` in the
    42    `grind` attributes; `fW.abortᵢ` for each `none` leaf, `fW.k_g.none` for each continuation (no
    43    patterns);
    44  * the **spec** `⦃s = s₀⦄ invoke p (exec p n) "f" args ⦃LocEq s' s₀ ∧
    45    fW n s₀.mem args = some (r.headD 0, s'.mem); ⊤⦄` of every member (`some (r, s'.mem)` for a list
    46    model, `some (r.headD 0, r.tail.headD 0, …, s'.mem)` for a tuple model), as one conjunction
    47    over the group (`name`), a step theorem per member (`name.stepᵢ`: `vcgen` with the specs of the
    48    callees and loops that member calls, then `finish`) and the induction on the fuel.
    49  
    50  The definitions come in dependency order: each strongly connected component of the reference
    51  graph is one definition or one `mutual` block, well-founded on `(fuel, depth)` if it has a
    52  continuation or a loop (models `(n, D)`, continuations `(n + 1, d)`, loops `(n, d)`; `LevelLeq.lean`
    53  does this by hand), structural on the fuel if it has only models.
    54  
    55  ```
    56  l_model liftGo_spec (p : Prog) (hp : LiftProg p)
    57    fns [(hp.get "lift_go") ↦ liftW, (hp.get "lift_app") ↦ liftAppW]
    58    specs [derB_spec p (hp.get "der_b") n, memoFindG_spec lfSch p _ (hp.get "lf_find") n]
    59    grind [arena_grind] fold [tierW, idxW] finish [tierW, idxW] gen 20 heartbeats 1000000
    60  ```

== ConAgua/Arena/ArenaRel.lean#L273-L296
   273  /-- **The arena relation**: every represented table and the pool (the store tier, over
   274  `a.store`), and the memo tier as one nested group over `a.memos`, on the one layout above. Kept
   275  opaque to `grind` (DESIGN.md, "Does the relation scale?"): proofs name its fields. -/
   276  structure ArenaR (m : Mem) (a : AState) : Prop where
   277    lit : LitR m a
   278    app : AppR m a
   279    sort : SortR m a
   280    const : ConstR m a

   282    bvar : BVarR m a
   283    fvar : FVarR m a
   284    lam : LamR m a
   285    forallE : ForallR m a
   286    proj : ProjR m a
   287    zero : ZeroR m a
   288    succ : SuccR m a
   289    max : MaxR m a

   291    param : ParamR m a

== ConAgua/Arena/ConsLibRel.lean#L6-L26
     6  /-!
     7  # The cons-table library: the relation and the user API (lane conslib)
     8  
     9  A cons table `C` (`ConsLib.lean`) represents the arena's two `Tbl`s of one constructor (the twin's
    10  `HashMap2`s: persistent and scratch) by **`ConsR C R m on P Q`**: both tiers hold the same nodes
    11  in the same order (node `i` of tier `t` related to `nodes[i]` by the instance's record relation
    12  `R`), the same key → handle map, the node counts at `CTL[ca + t]`, the scratch flag `CTL[1]` is
    13  `on`; and the slots index the nodes (the slot layout, the probing and the growth state, which no
    14  user sees). The L model of every `intern_X` is `consInternM C m ks` (`ConsLibSpec.lean`).
    15  
    16  Both are irreducible outside this file: the lemmas below are the whole interface.
    17  
    18  * **Reading the relation**: `ConsR.flag`, `ConsR.ctl`, `ConsR.cnt`, `ConsR.cap`, `ConsR.rec`,
    19    `ConsR.cons`, `ConsR.back`, `ConsR.recSize`, `ConsR.node`, `ConsR.cons_hit`.
    20  * **Keeping it**: `ConsR.frame` (a writer apart from the table), `ConsR.setFlag` (`CTL[1]`),
    21    `ConsR.reset` (the scratch reset), `consR_init` (the all-zero memory), `ConsR.congr`.
    22  * **An interning**: `consIntern_correct` (it refines the arena's hash-consing, from the
    23    instance's obligations `ConsKeyOK`), `consInternM_frame` (what it writes), `consInternM_word`,
    24    `consInternM_lt`, `consInternM_pw` (the handle word), `consInternM_out` (a hit, or the append
    25    of node `cntC`: the memory outside the slot array is `pushRec`).
    26  

== ConAgua/L/WriteSet.lean#L7-L24
     7  /-!
     8  # Write sets from the program text
     9  
    10  `Preserve.lean` proves once that a program without `st8` keeps the byte arrays and the sizes.
    11  The same induction gives a frame for every function of a *call-closed* set `fs` whose bodies
    12  store only into word arrays of `A` and into words of the control array `ctl` listed in `C`. A
    13  `ctl` index must be a literal `k`, or `k + (e &&& 1)`, which can only be `k` or `k + 1` (the
    14  tier-indexed counts of the stores, `CTL[k + (t & 1)]`). The check `closedW` is a `Bool` function
    15  of the text, so a concrete program's write set is `by decide +kernel`.
    16  
    17  The frame itself is abstract here (`WFrame`): any reflexive relation on memories closed under
    18  the allowed stores. `Arena/Frame.lean` instantiates it with `MemFrame` (the arena's layout:
    19  `CTL` is array 1). Lane `scale`'s spike, made layout-agnostic (DESIGN.md, "The relation's architecture").
    20  
    21  Global variables (`GVar`) are not restricted by `closedW` (a `WFrame` is closed under every global
    22  write). Their write sets are lists of names, `closedG p G fs` (section "Global variables" below):
    23  every run of `f ∈ fs` keeps the globals outside `G` (`GFrame`), and `Triple.gframe` adds that to a
    24  callee's spec for its caller's `vcgen`.

== ConAgua/L/Agree.lean#L570-L574
   570  /-- **Non-interference for `L.run`.** -/
   571  theorem run_agree {p : Prog} {S S8 : ArrId → Bool} {fs : List FnName}
   572      (hp : readsIn p S S8 fs = true) {f : FnName} (hf : f ∈ fs) (n : Nat) (vs : List Word)
   573      {m₁ m₂ : Mem} (hm : Agree S S8 m₁ m₂) :
   574      RunAgree S S8 (run p n f vs m₁) (run p n f vs m₂) := by

== ConAgua/L/Agree.lean#L7-L31
     7  /-!
     8  # Non-interference: runs that read only agreeing arrays agree
     9  
    10  `readsIn p S S8 fs` is a `Bool` check of the program text: every function of `fs` that `p`
    11  defines calls only into `fs`, and every array its body names (loaded, stored, measured, copied
    12  from or to, scanned) is a word array of `S` or a byte array of `S8`. The array sets are
    13  predicates (`S S8 : ArrId → Bool`; a list `l` is `l.contains`). A tiered access
    14  `a⟨t⟩` names both tiers, `a` and `a + tierOff`. Global variables are not restricted.
    15  (`Stmt.rdOk` takes the callee set as a predicate too: `readsIn` uses membership in `fs`, the
    16  per-function split for a large program (`Compiler/ReadSetSplit.lean`) a tree of name codes.)
    17  
    18  `Agree S S8 m₁ m₂`: the two memories have the same word arrays in `S`, the same byte arrays in
    19  `S8`, and the same globals. Everything else (other arrays, the number of arrays) may differ.
    20  
    21  **The theorem** (`invoke_agree`): for `f ∈ fs` of a set that passes `readsIn`, two runs of
    22  `invoke p (exec p n) f vs` from states that agree (memories `Agree`, equal locals) end the same
    23  way: the same error, or the same returned values from final states that agree again. `run_agree`
    24  is the same for `L.run`. The proof is the frame proof's induction (fuel, then statements): every
    25  read sees equal data, every write writes equal data to an array of `S`/`S8` (or a global).
    26  
    27  Why: lane parmode (docs/design/parmode.md, Step 4, piece (b2)). A worker runs `check_pending`
    28  in a memory in which only the frozen images and the worker's own arrays have content; every other
    29  array is empty. That memory agrees with the full sequential memory on `S` = frozen ∪ owned, so
    30  the worker's run is the sequential one, which the sequential proof covers.
    31  -/

== ConAgua/Checker/Pipeline.lean#L41-L45
    41  /-- **A relational stage spec**: from memory satisfying `Pre`, a returning call of `f` keeps the
    42  caller's locals and ends in memory satisfying `Post r`. -/
    43  def RelSpec (p : Prog) (f : FnName) (Pre : Mem → Prop) (Post : List Word → Mem → Prop) : Prop :=
    44    ∀ (n : Nat), n ≤ 2 ^ 62 → ∀ (s₀ : St), Pre s₀.mem → ⦃fun s => s = s₀⦄ invoke p (exec p n) f []
    45      ⦃fun r s' => LocEq s' s₀ ∧ Post r s'.mem; ⊤⦄

   132  theorem foldStage_checker (b pb : ByteArray) (s8 s64 : List Nat) (hin : InputsOK b pb s64)

   141        installFold .verified ipins (0, mkIFEnv IEnv.empty, #[]) ds.toList sE = .ok (.ok (ds.size, fe, pend), sF) ∧

== ConAgua/Checker/Pipeline.lean#L66-L69
    66  /-- What every stage may assume of the inputs: a 64-bit platform, both buffers below `2^63`
    67  bytes, every word array below `2^64` words. -/
    68  def InputsOK (b pb : ByteArray) (s64 : List Nat) : Prop :=
    69    System.Platform.numBits = 64 ∧ b.size < 2 ^ 63 ∧ pb.size < 2 ^ 63 ∧ ∀ n ∈ s64, n < 2 ^ 64

== ConAgua/Compiler/Compile.lean#L8-L26
     8  /-!
     9  # The naive compiler from L to Kraken x64
    10  
    11  See DESIGN.md, "The compiler". One pass, no register allocation: an expression is evaluated into
    12  `rax`, with intermediate values in fixed per-frame temporary slots.
    13  
    14  **Machine state during L code.**
    15  * `r15` = `T`, the address of the run's descriptor table (`Tab`); pinned.
    16  * `r14` = the fuel counter; decremented at every loop back-edge and every call.
    17  * `rsp` = the current frame; constant while a body runs. Local `x` is the word at `rsp + 8x`,
    18    temporary `t` is at `rsp + 8(nlocals + t)`. The frame has `frameWords` words.
    19  * `rbp` = the trampoline's saved stack pointer; never written by L code.
    20  * `rbx`, `r12`, `r13`: free; the trampoline saves and restores them for its caller.
    21  * `rax` = expression result, `rcx`/`rdx` = scratch, `rsi` = argument pointer at a call.
    22  
    23  **Exits.** `ca_error` and `ca_exhausted` are global; they restore the caller's `rsp` from `rbp`
    24  and return to the harness with `rdx` = 2 resp. 1. A normal return has `rdx` = 0 and the result
    25  in `rax`.
    26  -/

== ConAgua/Compiler/Compile.lean#L1194-L1214
  1194  def trampoline (tab : Tab) (entry : FnName) (c np : Nat) : Program :=
  1195    [.label enterL,
  1196     movMR (mb .rdi (tab.save np)) .r15, movMR (mb .rdi (tab.save np + 8)) .rbx,
  1197     movMR (mb .rdi (tab.save np + 16)) .r12, movMR (mb .rdi (tab.save np + 24)) .r13,
  1198     i64 (.push (oR .rbp)), i64 (.push (oR .r14)), i64 (.push (oR .rdi)),
  1199     movRR .rbp .rsp, movRR .r15 .rdi, movRR .r14 .rsi,
  1200     movRM .rsp (mb .r15 Tab.stackTop),
  1201     i64 (.lea (rr .rsi) (mb .r15 tab.args))] ++
  1202    (if np ≤ argRegs.length then loadArgs tab 0 (argRegs.take np) else []) ++ burnFuel ++
  1203    [i64 (.call (.rel (.sub (.label (fnL entry)) .after_current_instruction))),
  1204     jmpL okL,
  1205     .label exhaustedL, movRI .rdx 1, jmpL finishL,
  1206     .label errorL, movRI .rdx 2,
  1207     .label finishL, movRR .rsp .rbp,
  1208     i64 (.pop (.reg (rr .r15))),
  1209     movRM .rbx (mb .r15 (tab.save np + 8)), movRM .r12 (mb .r15 (tab.save np + 16)),
  1210     movRM .r13 (mb .r15 (tab.save np + 24)), movRM .r15 (mb .r15 (tab.save np)),
  1211     i64 (.pop (.reg (rr .r14))), i64 (.pop (.reg (rr .rbp))),
  1212     i64 .ret,
  1213     .label okL] ++ loadRes { tab, fn := entry, nl := 0, brk := okL } 0 c (tab.nres - c) ++
  1214    [movRI .rdx 0, jmpL finishL]

== ConAgua/Compiler/Compile.lean#L403
   403  def allocRegs : List Reg64 := [.rdi, .r8, .r9, .r10, .r11, .rsi, .rbx, .r12, .r13]

== ConAgua/Compiler/Compile.lean#L67-L81
    67  /-- The number of word arrays with both tiers in the table (`a` and `a + tierOff` below `nw`). -/
    68  def Tab.wK (t : Tab) : Nat := min (t.nw - tierOff) tierOff
    69  /-- The position of word array `a`'s descriptor words (lane tiercost): a permutation of
    70  `[0, nw)` that puts tier `1` of a tiered array right after tier `0` (`wpos (a + tierOff) =
    71  wpos a + 1` for `a < wK`), so that a tiered access addresses `[r15 + 8 (t & 1) + d]`. -/
    72  def Tab.wpos (t : Tab) (a : ArrId) : Nat :=
    73    if a < t.wK then 2 * a
    74    else if a < tierOff then a + t.wK
    75    else if a < tierOff + t.wK then 2 * (a - tierOff) + 1
    76    else a
    77  /-- The array whose descriptor words are at position `p` (`wpos`'s inverse). -/
    78  def Tab.wposInv (t : Tab) (p : Nat) : ArrId :=
    79    if p < 2 * t.wK then (if p % 2 = 0 then p / 2 else tierOff + p / 2)
    80    else if p < tierOff + t.wK then p - t.wK
    81    else p

== ConAgua/Compiler/Step.lean#L10-L18
    10  /-!
    11  # One instruction at a time
    12  
    13  The compiler proof is a forward simulation on Kraken's own judgment
    14  `Eventually (step1 Host.exe) Q ⟨d, pc⟩` ("every run from `d` at `pc` reaches `Q`"), for an
    15  arbitrary `Host` program that contains the compiled code. Each lemma here steps over one
    16  instruction form the compiler emits, in continuation-passing style: the hypothesis is the
    17  `Eventually` at the next state, the conclusion the `Eventually` at this one.
    18  -/

== ConAgua/Compiler/Rel.lean#L103-L122
   103  /-- L's memory `m` in the machine's data memory `d`. -/
   104  structure MemRel (G : Layout) (m : Mem) (d : DataMem) : Prop where
   105    nb : m.bytes.size = G.tab.nb
   106    nw : m.words.size = G.tab.nw
   107    size8 : ∀ a < G.tab.nb, (m.arr8 a).size = G.s8 a

   110    get64 : ∀ a < G.tab.nw, ∀ (i : Nat) (h : i < (m.arr64 a).size),
   111      rdW d (A (G.b64 a + 8 * i)) = some (m.arr64 a)[i]
   112    limit : rdW d (A (G.T + 8)) = some (UInt64.ofNat G.lo)

   114    len8 : ∀ a < G.tab.nb, rdW d (A (G.T + (G.tab.len8 a).toNat)) = some (UInt64.ofNat (G.s8 a))
   115    base64 : ∀ a < G.tab.nw, rdW d (A (G.T + (G.tab.base64 a).toNat)) = some (UInt64.ofNat (G.b64 a))
   116    len64 : ∀ a < G.tab.nw, rdW d (A (G.T + (G.tab.len64 a).toNat)) = some (UInt64.ofNat (G.s64 a))
   117    rom : ∀ (i : Nat) (h : i < G.tab.rom.length),

   119    stack : ∀ x, G.InStack x → (d.get? (A x)).isSome
   120    res : ∀ x, G.InRes x → (d.get? (A x)).isSome

== ConAgua/Compiler/Rel.lean#L66-L78
    66  /-- The regions are inside the address space and pairwise disjoint. -/
    67  structure Ok : Prop where
    68    tab_end : G.tabEnd < 2 ^ 64
    69    hi_le : G.hi < 2 ^ 64
    70    lo_le : G.lo ≤ G.hi
    71    end8 : ∀ a < G.tab.nb, G.b8 a + G.s8 a < 2 ^ 64

    77    arr64_disj : ∀ a < G.tab.nw, ∀ b < G.tab.nw, a ≠ b → ∀ x, G.In64 a x → ¬ G.In64 b x

== ConAgua/Compiler/Abi.lean#L8-L32
     8  # The entry stubs (lane `abi`)
     9  
    10  The harness's whole job shrinks to: map a zero region, hand over the two input buffers, call
    11  `ca_start(in, in_len, pins, pins_len, base, base_len)` once. `ca_start` is the sequential driver
    12  (`parStub`, below): it calls entry 1 and then entry 2 on the same region. Both go through the
    13  setup stub `ca_setup` (`abiStub`, an internal label; the argument registers as `ca_start`'s),
    14  emitted before the trampoline, which sets up inside the region everything the harness used to lay
    15  out (`L.Compiler.Tab`), then tail-jumps into the trampoline `ca_enter(T, fuel)`:
    16  
    17  * System V arguments: `rdi`/`rsi` = the input bytes (byte array `0`), `rdx`/`rcx` = the pin-data
    18    bytes (byte array `1`; ignored if the program has one byte array), `r8` = `base`, `r9` =
    19    `base_len`. Returns `rax`/`rdx` as `ca_enter` does.
    20  * If `base_len < abiNeed`, it returns at once with `rdx = 1` (resources exhausted; never accept).
    21  * The region is a static partition into `abiSlot`-byte slots (no allocator; the pages that are
    22    never touched never become real): slot `0` is the table (`T = base`), slot `1` the L stack
    23    (`abiStack` bytes at its bottom), then one slot per byte array `2, …, nb - 1` and per word array.
    24    Each array starts at its slot's start; its length is `abiSlot` bytes, resp. `abiWords` words.
    25  * The constant data is written into the table by immediate stores (no `.rodata` read); the result
    26    area and the global variables are the region's zeros.
    27  * The fuel is `2^62 - 1` (`compile_correct` takes any `N < 2^62`).
    28  
    29  Nothing here is trusted: `sim_abiStub` (`ConAgua/Compiler/AbiSim.lean`) runs the stub on the
    30  machine, `abiLayout_ok` and `abi_memRel` (`ConAgua/Final/Abi.lean`) show that it establishes
    31  `Layout.Ok`/`MemRel` for the partition, and `abi_harness` gives `compile_correct`'s premises at
    32  the trampoline. -/

    17  /-- **The checker's code**: the `.text` section of `checker.s`. -/
    18  noncomputable def checkerFile : Program := include_asm "../checker.s"

== ConAgua/Checker/Asm.lean#L12-L21
    12  /-!
    13  # The checker's machine code, as a kernel-checked literal (generated by `scripts/checker_prog.py`; do not edit)
    14  
    15  `checkerAsm : Program` is the compiled checker as a literal term, and
    16  `checkerAsm_eq : compileProg checkerTab checkerProg "check" = checkerAsm` is checked by the kernel,
    17  one function at a time (`asm_lit`, `ConAgua/Compiler/AsmLit.lean`; the functions' checks are in
    18  `AsmPart0` … `AsmPart9`), so running the compiler as compiled Lean code is not trusted.
    19  `checkerFile_eq` (`ConAgua/Checker/AsmFileEq.lean`) compares it with the committed file
    20  `checker.s` (`scripts/asm_file.py`). DESIGN.md, "Kernel-checked compiler output".
    21  -/

== ConAgua/AsmFile/Include.lean#L6-L25
     6  # `include_asm "path"`: an assembler file as a `Program` (TRUSTED)
     7  
     8  `include_asm "path"` is a term of type `Program`: the `.text` section of the assembler file at
     9  `path` (relative to the directory of the current Lean file, as `include_str`), read by
    10  `parseAsmFile` (`ConAgua/AsmFile/Parse.lean`) when the term is elaborated, and turned into a term by
    11  `programTerm` (`ConAgua/AsmFile/Term.lean`). A file it cannot parse is an error.
    12  
    13  The term is cut into segments for the kernel's sake, without changing its value: a new segment
    14  starts at the label `ca_enter` (the trampoline) and at each function entry `ca_f_g`; the labels of
    15  segment `ca_f_g` are written as `lbl "g" n m` where that is their value. So the term is
    16  `stub ++ (trampoline ++ (f₀ ++ (… ++ (fₖ ++ []))))`, the shape `asm_lit`'s `checkerAsm` has.
    17  
    18  The trusted base is this parser (`parseAsmFile`): the term comes from it alone. Two independent
    19  cross-checks, not needed for soundness: Kraken's own parser must read the file's code the same way
    20  (`ConAgua/AsmFile/CrossCheck.lean`, run by `scripts/asm_file.py`: ~13 s, too slow to
    21  run here), and the assembler must encode what the file says (`scripts/check-asm.sh`). And here,
    22  the code is printed again with Kraken's printer (`toATT`) and compared with the file's `.text`
    23  lines: parse ∘ print is the identity on the file, so the parser reads every instruction the way
    24  the printer (which wrote the file) meant it.
    25  

== ConAgua/AsmFile/CrossCheck.lean#L5-L11
     5  /-! `lake env lean --run ConAgua/AsmFile/CrossCheck.lean FILE.s`: reads the file's code with both
     6  parsers, the trusted one (`parseAsmFile`, `ConAgua/AsmFile/Parse.lean`, which the final theorems'
     7  term comes from) and Kraken's own (`Kraken.X64.Parser.parse`, independent code), and fails
     8  (exit 1), naming the first differing directive, its line and function, if they disagree. A
     9  cross-check, not part of the trusted base; `scripts/asm_file.py` runs it. It is
    10  not in `include_asm`: Kraken's parser takes about 17 s on the checker's 5.3 MB there, twice the
    11  module's elaboration time (docs/design/asmfile.md). -/

== scripts/asm_file.py#L2-L21
     2  """Regenerate the two committed generated files the binary is built from (`make`, `Makefile`):
     3  
     4  * `checker.s`: the entry stub, the trampoline and the compiled checker, printed by
     5    `ConAgua/Checker/AsmEmit.lean` (run as a script, so the compiler runs as compiled Lean code;
     6    nothing here is trusted: the final theorems are about the file as the trusted parser reads it
     7    (`ConAguaAsm/Checker.lean`), and the kernel checks that it is the compiler's output,
     8    `checkerFile_eq` in `ConAgua/Checker/AsmFileEq.lean`). Regenerate after every change to the
     9    checker's L code (`ConAgua/Checker/Prog.lean`), the compiler or the stub.
    10  * `pins.bin`: the pin data `main.c` embeds, written by `romgen pins.bin 3`
    11    (`ConAgua/Rom/Gen.lean`): the checker's startup data and all of con-leche's `natOpPinSets` (3
    12    variants, the set con-ron embeds). Not trusted either: the theorems hold for every pin buffer.
    13    Regenerate after a change to the startup data or a twin bump.
    14  
    15  Both modes also run the parser cross-check `ConAgua/AsmFile/CrossCheck.lean` on `checker.s`:
    16  Kraken's own parser must read the code as the trusted parser does (~13 s; not in `include_asm`,
    17  where it would double the module's elaboration time).
    18  
    19  Usage: scripts/asm_file.py [--check] [--no-build]
    20    --check     fail (exit 1) if a file would change; do not write it
    21    --no-build  do not build ConAgua.Checker.AsmEmit's imports and romgen first"""

== ConAgua/Final/TwinPooled.lean#L3-L13
     3  /-!
     4  # The twin's pipeline with phase B as con-ron's pool (lane parmode)
     5  
     6  The threaded mode checks the pending groups on several workers; what its accept means on the twin
     7  side is con-ron's `PooledAccepts` (`ConRon/Arena/Pooled.lean`): phase A accepted, and a family of
     8  group lists covering every pending group, each accepted by `checkPendingList` from the phase-A

    11  theorem of type `False`) are `Twin.lean`'s, through Theorem 1 for the pool
    12  (`Arena.pooledAccepts_bridge`), which is what `twinAccepts_pure` already uses.

== ConAgua/Checker/Entry.lean#L109-L124
   109  /-- `check_b()`: on the worker region's first call the seed (`CTL`) from the buffer, then the
   110  pending groups `PLO‥PHI-1` (`PHI` at most the count) at phase A's final view, in order, as phase
   111  B's loop (`check_pending_go`); returns `ACCEPT`. -/
   112  -- con-ron: ConRon/Arena/Phased.lean:29-36 ConRon.Arena.AState.worker
   113  -- con-ron: ConRon/Arena/Pooled.lean:30-43 ConRon.Arena.PooledAccepts
   114  def checkBL : FunDecl := lfn () locals (z, n) {
   115    if INIT == 0 {
   116      n := len(CTLF.u64);
   117      copy!(CTL.u64, 0, CTLF.u64, 0, n);
   118      INIT := 1
   119    };
   120    if CTL.u64[130] < PHI { abort };
   121    if PHI < PLO { abort };
   122    z := call check_pending_go(PLO, PHI, HDRF.u64[3]);
   123    return 71757147230292
   124  }

== ConAgua/Compiler/Abi.lean#L157-L166
   157  * `ca_start(in, in_len, pins, pins_len, base, base_len)` (**the sequential driver**, what the
   158    harness calls): entry 1 with the mode word `3` (`ca_start_a0`: the buffer's header only); if it
   159    returns `rdx = 0` and `rax = 2^63 + k`, `ca_check_seq` on the same region for `[0, k)`, whose
   160    result is the result. It needs no more memory than `ca_setup`: entry 2 runs on phase A's region,
   161    on the arrays as phase A left them.
   162    It keeps its return address and the caller's `r15` past `ca_setup`'s region (`drvSave`; the
   163    driver's region is 16 bytes larger, `drvNeed`, the size `ca_region_size` names), pops its return
   164    address off the machine stack before each `call` and holds `base` in `r15` (which `ca_enter`
   165    restores); so each callee's machine stack is the caller's (the 32 bytes `AbiCall` names) and
   166    the driver touches no callee-saved register but `r15`. -/

== main.c#L129-L144
   129  /* `--jobs=N` (N > 1), the threaded mode.
   130  
   131     Entry 1 (`ca_start_a`) runs the stages and phase A in the region. On success (rdx = 0,
   132     rax = 2^63 + k, k pending groups) it has written the frozen buffer into the array `OUT`, whose
   133     word 1 is the buffer's length in words. The buffer stays where it is: the rest of the region is
   134     unmapped around it and the buffer is made read-only, so a write to it faults and kills the
   135     process, which is never an accept (route A). N threads then each map their own zero region of
   136     ca_worker_size bytes and claim group indices from one atomic counter, calling
   137     `ca_check_b(buf, len, j, region, region_len)` for each claimed j, one call after the other on
   138     the region as the previous call left it.
   139  
   140     Concurrency: the threads share only the read-only buffer, the claim counter (fetch_add hands
   141     out each of 0, 1, 2, ... once) and a stop flag that only shortens a failing run. Each thread
   142     has its own region and its own result slot; main combines the slots after joining every
   143     thread. Accept iff every slot is 0: every call that thread made accepted, and the threads drain
   144     the counter past k unless one fails. */

== ConAgua/Final/EndToEnd.lean#L122-L128
   122  /-- **Threaded accept**: if the harness runs as `ThreadsRun` says (entry 1, then `ca_check_b` per
   123  claimed group index on each thread's own region, every call accepting, every index claimed), the
   124  twin's pooled pipeline accepts `[b]`. -/

   128      (hR : ThreadsRun b pb dm₀ ra₀ st₀ B ths) : TwinAcceptsPooled [b] :=
